caption_hook: Ohio has been scraped by glaciers, lapped by tropical seas and ruled by a giant armored fish.

layers.name: GLACIAL TILL
layers.what: Ice sheets pushed down from the north and left a thick blanket of clay, sand and boulders over much of Ohio. On Lake Erie's Kelleys Island the ice also carved giant grooves into the limestone below.
layers.bonus: Kelleys Island's Glacial Grooves rank among the largest in the world.

layers.name: BLACK HAND SANDSTONE
layers.what: Rivers laid down thick beds of coarse sand that hardened into soft sandstone. Wind and water have since carved it into recess caves, gorges and waterfalls.
layers.bonus: Black Hand Gorge near Newark is named for a Native American rock carving of a black hand.

layers.name: BEREA SANDSTONE
layers.hook: Sand from an ancient river delta
layers.what: Rivers dumped sand into a shallow sea, building a delta that hardened into sandstone. Quarried around Berea and Amherst, it was cut into grindstones and building blocks.
layers.bonus: Amherst, Ohio, calls itself the Sandstone Capital of the World.

layers.name: CLEVELAND SHALE
layers.hook: Home of the armored sea monster
layers.what: A warm sea covered Ohio, its bottom starved of oxygen, which left black mud that became shale. It holds Dunkleosteus, a giant armored fish with bladelike jaw plates instead of teeth.
layers.bonus: Dunkleosteus fossils are found in Cleveland's rivers and creeks.

layers.name: WAYNESVILLE FORMATION
layers.what: Alternating limestone and shale from a shallow sea crowd with fossils: lampshells, corals and trilobites. Collectors dig them at Caesar Creek and in hillsides around Cincinnati.
layers.bonus: The trilobite Isotelus is Ohio's official state fossil, found around Cincinnati.
